issues.evidence: Tibetan འཛིན་པ་མེད་པར་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་གསུངས་ན: the Tathagata spoke of it as 'without grasping' (Skt agrāha); the translation reverses the negation. Chone Drakpa 2-133 says the Tathagata has abandoned it and has no such clinging.
Tibetan ཁྲི་དགུ་སྟོང་ = 9,000 x 10,000 = ninety million (English: ninety million). 九百萬 is only nine million.

Tibetan དེ་འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་པར་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་གསུངས་ (Skt asaṃjñā): the Tathagata spoke of it as 'no perception'. The translation affirms a 'real perception' instead, adding content and reversing the sense.
Tibetan མར་མེ་མཛད (Skt Dīpaṃkara) is the Buddha from whom nothing was obtained; the locked term is 燃燈佛. Shakyamuni is the Tathagata who speaks. Chone Drakpa 2-51 and Kamalaśīla 3-95 name Dipamkara.
Tibetan དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་མཁྱེན་ཏོ and Skt jñātās te ... tathāgatena: the Tathagata knows them. The translation negates it.
Tibetan མི་གནས་པར་སྦྱིན་པ་སྦྱིན་པ (Skt apratiṣṭhito dānaṃ dadāti): gives without abiding (locked 不住). The translation says the opposite, 'abiding'.
Tibetan མདོ་སྡེ་འདི་བཤད་པ་ལ ('when this sūtra is being explained'; Skt sūtre bhāṣyamāṇe) is missing; the translation states only 'those who are not frightened'.
issues.fix: 凡是在宣說此經時不驚恐、不害怕、不極度畏懼的眾生，將具備最極稀有

issues.span: 佛允諾諸菩薩摩訶薩往生其淨土
issues.evidence: Nothing in the Tibetan or Sanskrit about promising rebirth in a pure land; the Tibetan only says the Tathagata benefited (ཕན་གདགས་པ) the bodhisattvas. Chone Drakpa 2-3 explains benefit through Dharma and entrusting, with no pure land.
issues.fix: 如來以所有最勝的饒益來饒益諸菩薩摩訶薩

issues.span: 世尊、如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者，佛
issues.evidence: The epithets 'Tathagata, arhat, perfectly complete Buddha' are the agent of the benefiting (ཀྱིས); the vocative bhagavan is separate. The Chinese lists them as parallel vocatives and then adds a separate subject 佛, obscuring the agent.
issues.fix: 世尊！如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者

issues.evidence: Tibetan མཚན་སུམ་ཅུ་རྩ་གཉིས (Skt dvātriṃśan) = thirty-two marks; locked term 三十二相.
Tibetan སྲོག (Skt jīva) has locked rendering 壽者; 靈魂 'soul' is a different concept. Chone Drakpa 2-113 lists སེམས་ཅན, སྲོག, གང་ཟག as the three.
Tibetan མི་བཟོད་དོ (Skt na kṣamate): does not bear comparison/does not withstand. The Chinese says it can be compared, reversing the sense.

issues.span: 將某些法施設為毀壞，亦施設為斷滅
issues.evidence: Tibetan ཆོས་གང་ཡང་རྣམ་པར་བཤིག་པའམ་ཆད་པར་བཏགས་པ་མེད་དོ (Skt na ... kasyacid dharmasya vināśaḥ prajñapto nocchedaḥ): they do NOT designate any phenomenon as destroyed or annihilated. The translation affirms it and turns 'or' into 'and also'.
issues.fix: 不將任何法施設為毀壞或斷滅

issues.evidence: Tibetan ཆོས་སུ་འདུ་ཤེས་པ་དང༌། ཆོས་མེད་པར་ཡང་འདུ་ཤེས་མི་འཇུག: the negation མི་འཇུག governs both perceptions (Skt nāpi ... dharmasaṃjñā pravartate, evaṃ nādharmasaṃjñā). The translation affirms the perception of a phenomenon.
issues.fix: 也不會生起法想，也不會生起非法想

issues.evidence: Tibetan སྔ་དྲོའི་དུས (Skt pūrvāhṇa) means morning; 傍晚 is evening.

issues.span: 確實有教法可以被緣取為所謂說法
issues.evidence: Tibetan ཆོས་དེ་གང་ཡང་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར (Skt nāsti sa kaścid dharmaḥ): there is no phenomenon that can be apprehended as 'teaching the Dharma'. The translation asserts existence.
issues.fix: 是因為沒有任何教法可以被緣取為所謂說法的緣故

issues.evidence: Tibetan ཟིལ་བ (Skt avaśyāya) is dew, locked as 露; 彩虹 (rainbow) is a different item.
Tibetan བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ requires the locked rendering 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提; the rendered phrase also duplicates 等覺 with 現等覺.
Tibetan ཆོས་རྣམས་ཀྱང་སྤང་བར་བྱ (Skt dharmā eva prahātavyāḥ): even phenomena should be abandoned, let alone non-phenomena. The translation says to hold on to them, reversing the sense.
